t: Founded around 1528 by a son of the last Sultan of Malacca, Johor claimed Malacca's royal line and maritime empire.
It allied with the Dutch to take Malacca in 1641 and became the leading Malay entrepôt of the late seventeenth century.
Its partition by Britain and the Netherlands in 1824 created modern borders; it survives as a monarchy within Malaysia.
dyk: Johor's constitution of 1895, issued under Sultan Abu Bakar, forbade any ruler from surrendering the state or any part of it to a foreign power.
ev: Alauddin Riayat Shah II founds a new court on the Johor River
Aceh sacks Johor's capital Batu Sawar
Johor and the Dutch take Malacca from the Portuguese
Sultan Mahmud Shah II is murdered, ending the Malacca line
Raffles recognises Hussein as sultan and founds British Singapore
The Anglo-Dutch Treaty splits the realm; Riau-Lingga goes to the Dutch sphere
Britain recognises Abu Bakar as Sultan of Johor
Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar becomes King of Malaysia

f.capital: Johor Lama and Batu Sawar; later Riau; from 1866 Johor Bahru
